Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:30: And he said to you specifically, because her arousal toward unification depends on the lower ones, as he says (Song of Songs 8:13), "companions listen for your voice, let me hear it." And he said "inun de-tiuvta dilhon" - meaning, those whose soul desires the Shechinah, like a man who pursues the object of his heart's desire, burning after her love, and cannot sleep from the abundance of his love for her - so too those who have the great desire for the Shechinah do not give rest to their heart, for from the abundance of their desire and the fire of love of the Shechinah burning in their heart, when they awaken from their sleep, sleep and laziness do not master them, but they rise with alacrity and joy and love of the Shechinah to unify her - because through her unification with her husband, who is YHVH, they are cleaved to YHVH, and their soul rejoices and delights to be cleaved to the supernal life, along the lines of "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" - the desire of the lower to be included in the upper, as explained. And this is "those who remind the LORD" [hamazkirim et Hashem] - "et" is the Shechinah, YHVH is the Holy One, blessed be He; and "mazkirim" is a term meaning binding and unification, along the lines of "azkaratah," which means incense, and incense is a bond, for the Aramaic translation of "bond" is "ketar."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:31: "Take no rest" - the reason has already been explained in chapter 4, because she sings forever, along the lines of his saying (Psalms 83:2), "O God, do not be silent" - and she depends on the lower ones, and therefore it says, "take no rest," so that she too shall not be silent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:32: And it appears worth examining precisely the wording of the verse, which does not say "give it no rest" in the form of a command, as it says elsewhere. And this matter is precise in the words of Rabbi Abba, the author of the discourse: "those whose desire is to remember the Holy One, blessed be He, give no rest," and so on - meaning, those whose custom already is that their desire and longing is to remember the Holy One, blessed be He - and this is "those who remind [remember] the LORD" - that you are already accustomed to remembering the LORD, so I need not command "take no rest," for the matter comes of itself, compelled by their abundant longing that they not give Him rest - and this is "give no rest," along the lines of "one commandment draws another commandment"; how much more does their desire to remember the LORD arouse in them that they not be silent and their heart not rest.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:33: And through this may be understood the plain sense of the verse (Isaiah 62:6), "on your walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen; all the day and all the night they shall never be silent" - and these are watchmen appointed above by decree, that they not be silent. But "those who remind the LORD" have a wondrous virtue, for they need no command, but of themselves "take no rest." Behold, one repair for the Shechinah - that one who conducts himself this way is certainly a great lover of her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:34: Further, in the rest of the Tikkunim: "when morning ascends, they hasten to the synagogue." And it says "hasten," this too concerning love - for from the abundance of their love to be bound to the Shechinah, they will run and hasten to the synagogue, as they say (Berachot, first chapter, 6b), it is a commandment to run to the synagogue, as it is said (Hosea 6:3), "then shall we know, if we pursue to know the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:35: It is also possible to say "they hasten" in order to be among the first ten, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot, first chapter, ibid.), a person should always rise early to the synagogue so that he merit to be counted among the first ten - and as explained in its secret in Parashat Naso (page 126a), and we shall explain further below. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 8a): Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, come early and stay late at the synagogue, so as to prolong your days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:36: And especially if he is the first in the synagogue - for Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Terumah, page 131a): whoever comes first becomes attached to the Shechinah and stands at the rank of the righteous, and the love of the King is performed for him - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:37: And in the Shacharit prayer we unify the Shechinah and bind her to Chesed - namely, Abraham instituted the Shacharit prayer. And after midday, which is the time of Mincha, when the sun has already declined, as is explained in the Gemara (Yoma 28b), "from when the walls begin to be shaded" - then Gevurah begins to be aroused, as is explained at the beginning of Parashat Naso (page 120a) - then is the time of the Mincha prayer, to unify the Shechinah in the left arm; Isaac instituted the Mincha prayer. And so at night is her unification in the middle line; Jacob instituted the evening prayer - namely (Genesis 28:11), "and he lodged there, for the sun had set" - for the sun came to her, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 224a, and also Parashat Vayetze, page 148a), concerning the matter of "and he took of the stones of the place and put them at his head."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:38: And in the Tikkunim (page 45a), in these words: in the Shacharit prayer, it ascends in the name called "El," "the great God" indeed; in the Mincha prayer, it ascends in the name called "Elohim"; in the evening prayer, it ascends in the name called YHVH - the secret of the matter (Psalms 50:1), "El, Elohim, YHVH, He spoke and called the earth" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:39: And he further says further on (page 45a) that through Netzach, Hod, and Yesod one ascends to be bound to the three Patriarchs, in these words: and further, "perfumed with myrrh" (Song of Songs 3:6), "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me" (ibid. 1:13) - this is Netzach, which ascends on the right, as it is written (Psalms 16:11), "pleasures in Your right hand forever [netzach]." And frankincense, this is Hod, which ascends into Gevurah. "From all the powders of the merchant" - this is Yesod [the Righteous One], which ascends into the middle pillar - to this point. Behold, it is explained from these discourses that the essence of our prayers is to unify the Shechinah forever in the aspects mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:40: Further, one must intend every day to unify the Shechinah in the secret of the bed, the table, the chair, and the menorah, which Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Terumah (page 133a), and we shall explain them, with God's help, in the matter of prayer. Behold, this is a comprehensive unification for the entirety of the day, and in the Gate of Prayer it will be explained how, in the Shacharit prayer, we draw the Shechinah toward us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:41: Further, there are three things a person should do every day to draw the Shechinah upon him: the first, donning tefillin; the second, occupation with Torah; and the third, giving her sustenance, clothing, and conjugal due.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:42: Concerning tefillin, they explained in the Tikkunim (page 2a) that they belong to the female [Nukva], and one who dons them is the sign of the covenant and the sign of tefillin, and he is a "son" - and concerning him it is said, "you shall not take the mother with the sons," for the Shechinah rests upon them forever. In these words: these are the ones who keep the sign of the covenant within its boundary of eight days, and keep the sign of Shabbat within its boundary, which are Y-Y Adonai - for whose sake the masters of the Mishnah established that no person is found lacking both of these, as it is written (Deuteronomy 22:6), "you shall not take the mother with the sons"; and those who are not found every day with these two signs, which are the sign of tefillin and the sign of the covenant of circumcision, and on Shabbat the sign of the covenant and the sign of Shabbat - of them it is written, "you shall in any case let go the mother"; and if you ask why both must be present in every person every day, it is so that the Shechinah, who is the yud of Adonai, not be found alone without the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the yud of YHVH, and a person must not be found lacking both of these every day. And if not, of him it is said (Proverbs 16:28), "and a slanderer separates the great one" - this separates the Master of the world from the Shechinah, the female, of whom it is said (Exodus 31:17), "it is a sign forever," while the male is "a covenant of salt forever" (Numbers 18:19); and therefore the tefillin are female, the covenant is male, and the secret of the matter, "mi ya'aleh lanu ha-shamaymah" (Deuteronomy 30:12), whose initial letters spell "milah" [circumcision] and final letters spell YHVH - in the tefillin, the female - this is what is written (Exodus 13:16), "and it shall be for a sign upon your hand [yad kehah - dim hand]" - to this point. And in the plain sense of his words is proof of our intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:43: Through occupation with Torah, they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayera, page 115b): Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosi were walking on the road. Rabbi Yehuda said to Rabbi Yosi, open your mouth and engage in Torah, for the Shechinah is found with you - for all the while words of Torah are engaged, the Shechinah comes and joins; and all the more so on the road, for the Shechinah goes first and comes and walks before those people who merit through faith in the Holy One, blessed be He - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:44: And so he also said in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 50a) that Torah scholars who separate from their wives all six weekdays - the Shechinah is with them, and they are male and female.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:45: Indeed, in order for the Shechinah to rest upon him, it is necessary that his study be in a fixed manner, not occasional - and so they explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (page 238b), in these words: and therefore, "if a bird's nest chances before you" [ki yikra kan tzippor] - occasionally, once, like a guest or lodger who happens by for a while at his lodging place; and there are those whose Torah is [their] dwelling for the Shechinah, this is what is written (Exodus 31:16), "and the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, le-dorotam" [for their generations] - "le-dirtam" lacking [a letter], meaning of dwelling; and there are masters of Mishnah whose Torah is their profession, from whom the Shechinah never departs all their days; but these, "if a bird's nest chances before you" - with them the Shechinah is only occasional, sometimes resting upon them and found with them, and sometimes not found with them. And the secret of the matter: sometimes she is found with them - "you shall not take the mother"; and sometimes she is not found - "you shall in any case let go the mother." Chicks - these are masters of Mishnah; or eggs - masters of Scripture; with those whose study is not fixed, "you shall in any case let go the mother"; but with those whose study is fixed, "you shall not take the mother with the sons" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:46: And so they explained in the Tikkunim (end of 21a): if so, what is "if a bird's nest chances before you"? Rather, at a time when the Shechinah has no fixed place to rest there, she goes by chance - and this is [the meaning of] "whoever fixes a place for his prayer" - just as souls behave, so the Shechinah rests with them: a soul that is fixed in prayer or in Torah is a fixed place for the Shechinah to rest in it, but a soul that has no fixedness in prayer or Torah, but it happens to it by chance - so she rests with it by chance, and this is "if a bird's nest chances before you." And so the soul of a person is called a bird's nest, and the body is the nest of the soul; and so souls that are her maidens, called "virgins after her, her companions," dwell in bodies that are their nests, occasionally, at a time when they are not fixed in synagogues and study houses - and this is "if a bird's nest chances before you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:47: Sustenance, clothing, and conjugal due - they explained in the Tikkunim (22a): and further, these ask for sustenance, and clothing, and conjugal due, which is the time of their union from Sabbath to Sabbath, of which it is said (Exodus 21:10), "her sustenance, her clothing, and her conjugal due he shall not diminish" - and there is none who asks for sustenance, which is the Shechinah's sustenance, and she is the supernal Mother, of whom it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "and do not forsake the Torah of your mother." Her clothing - this is the covering of the tzitzit and its wrapping, and the hand-tefillin, of which it is said (Psalms 102:1), "a prayer of the afflicted, when he wraps himself." And her conjugal due - this is the recitation of the Shema in its proper time. For if these three are not done for her, for the Shechinah, "then she shall go out for nothing, without payment" - she has no shame from the Shechinah; he is brazen. And further, "without payment" - he shall have no shame for the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:48: And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 49, page 100b) they explained these three in another manner, closer to the accepted view - they interpreted there "sustenance, clothing, and conjugal due" in the secret of three reincarnations [gilgulim], and afterward said: Rabbi Shimon said, old man, old man, speak more words, for these words of yours are concealed. That old man said to him: "her sustenance" - this is sustenance from the side of the right, from which all sustenance comes, this is what is written (Psalms 145:16), "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing" - this is the right hand. "Her clothing" - from the side of the left, which is the covering of the eyes, from which the left grows dim, because on the side of the north, the left, there is a flaw there, this is what is written (Jeremiah 1:14), "out of the north the evil shall break forth" - and therefore it is said of Isaac (Genesis 27:1), "and it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim from seeing" - and there a covering is needed; and of Moses it is said (Exodus 3:6), "and Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look upon God" - and therefore the tzitzit and tefillin are her coverings, this is what is written (Exodus 22:26), "for it alone is his covering, it is his garment for his skin" - "for his skin," referring to the leather of the tefillin; "his covering" - "upon the four corners of your covering with which you cover yourself" (ibid. 12:12) [sic, ref]. And "her conjugal due" - from the side of the middle pillar, which is Israel, "Hear O Israel" (Deuteronomy 6:4), and there is her unification; this is what is written (Exodus 21:11), "and if he does not do these three for her, then she shall go out for nothing, without payment" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:49: And what he said, that sustenance is nourishment from the side of the right, whereas above it was explained that it is Torah from the side of Binah - there is no difficulty at all in this, for even though sustenance is on the right, it flows from Binah, since "children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit, but on fortune [mazal]" - and they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 10, page 25b) that it is not dependent on merit, which is Chesed, but on fortune, which is Binah - see there. And so Torah too flows from Binah, as explained in Parashat Kedoshim, and comes to Chesed, and from there is sustenance to the Shechinah, and this is (Proverbs 31:26), "and the Torah of kindness is on her tongue."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:50: And incidentally we learn that the intent of the covering of tzitzit and tefillin is to conceal the Shechinah, and likewise the soul, from the powers of judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:51: Behold, the obligation incumbent upon every person is explained: to perform and repair every day sustenance, clothing, and conjugal due for the Shechinah - and through this his own soul is also repaired, for the soul is "a portion of YHVH," as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the portion of the LORD is His people," as we have explained several times - and when the Shechinah is repaired through him, she will certainly rest upon him, as it is said (Proverbs 8:17), "I love those who love me" - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, also explained the verse "from every man whose heart makes him willing," and so on, which we copied in chapter 4.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:52: And these four things we have explained are comprehensive unifications for every single day; there are still several particulars that will be explained, with God's help, each in its place. And of one who repairs his days always in the unification of the Shechinah as explained, it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:9), "enjoy life with the wife whom you love, all the days of your fleeting life," as we copied the discourse in the previous chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:53: And further concerning its virtue, they explained there in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz, page 196b): another interpretation, "with your strength" - this is the "woman" we spoke of, who is the strength to be made mighty by in this world and the World to Come, and a person must merit her in this world so as to be made mighty in that world. Why? Because after a person departs this world he has no strength to do anything, and to say "now, from here on I shall act" - certainly "there is no work, nor reckoning, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in Sheol, where you are going" (Ecclesiastes 9:10) - if a person does not merit in this world, he will not merit afterward in that world; and they established, whoever does not prepare provisions to depart from this world will not eat in that world; and there are good deeds a person does in this world from which he eats here, and all of it remains for the World to Come, to be nourished from them. Come and see: Joseph merited in this world and in the World to Come, because he wished to be unified with "a woman who fears the LORD," as it is written (Genesis 39:9), "and sin against God" - and because of this he merited to rule in this world, and he merited it for Israel - to this point, relevant here. And it is explained in the discourse how great is the virtue of one who holds fast to the Shechinah in his deeds, whether in this world or in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:54: And as a general rule, for all the unifications of the Shechinah that we have explained and shall further explain, with God's help, one must, before performing that unification, say with his mouth and utter with his lips: "this thing, or this commandment, I am doing to unify the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He" - and intend the unification of Y-A-K-D-O-N-K-Y [YHVH-Adonai], and intend that through this she shall be elevated from exile. How so? Going to the synagogue for the Shacharit prayer, he should say: I am going to unify the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the right arm - and intend the intention we explained - and so on for the other prayers and commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:55: And this matter is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tazria, page 51, at its end), and these are the words of Rabbi Elazar, in these words: Rabbi Elazar said, in all his deeds a person should desire that they all be for the holy Name - what is "for the holy Name"? To mention with his mouth the holy Name over everything he does, for it is all for His service, and the Other Side should not rest upon it - because it is always ready toward people and can rest upon that deed - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:56: And although the surface meaning of his words, as he said "over everything he does," refers to worldly deeds that are for His service - for if it is in the performance of the commandments, that is the service itself - nevertheless, it is possible that even in the performance of a commandment there be some ulterior motive, for the Examiner of hearts knows all; and when, at the start of the deed, he says with his mouth that it is for His service, for the sake of the Name of the LORD, with the intention to unify as explained, he thereby removes any external element from attaching to that commandment. And so it appears from his words that he said, "in all his deeds a person should desire" - and why does he include "all"? Surely, this is certainly its meaning: not only in words of holiness which one must mention [the Name], for the husk [kelipah] desires more to cling to the spirituality of the commandments than to a physical thing that has no substance - but even in worldly matters he should say "for the sake of the Name of the LORD," so that the husk not rest upon any of his physical deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:57: And so you will find that the custom of the ancients, peace be upon them, was to utter the intention with their mouths before performing the commandment - as with Rabbi Abba, peace be upon him, concerning the three Sabbath meals; in the Zohar they said (Parashat Yitro, page 88a), in these words: Rabbi Abba, when he sat at the Sabbath meal, would rejoice at each and every one, saying, "this is the meal of the Holy Ancient One," and so on; at another meal he would say, "this is the meal of the Holy One, blessed be He"; and so at all the meals - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:58: And so he himself said in the Zohar (Parashat Tazria, page 50a), in these words: come and see, it is written, "and all the women whose hearts stirred them" [ish - man; asher nasa liban]; at the time they performed the work, they would say, "this is for the Sanctuary, this is for the Tabernacle, this is for the curtain" - and so all those craftsmen, because holiness rested upon their hands and that work was sanctified; and when it ascended to its place, it ascended in holiness - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:59: And he further says afterward, that even in worldly matters one must mention [the Name], in these words: and therefore, whoever builds a building, when he begins to build, should mention that it is for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He - this is building a house, of which it is written (Jeremiah 22:13), "woe to him who builds his house without righteousness" - and then heavenly assistance rests upon him, and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares holiness for him, and calls upon him "peace," this is what is written (Job 5:24), "and you shall know that your tent is in peace" - what is "and you shall visit your habitation"? They have already established it; but "and you shall visit" means to commit the matter to speech when he builds, and then "you shall not sin" is written - to this point. And from this we may infer to all other worldly matters. And so Rav Hamnuna, concerning the sukkah, as they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, end of page 103) - see there - and from this we learn concerning the other commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:60: And it appears to me that concerning this it is said (Isaiah 62:6), "those who remind the LORD, take no rest" - that they should mention the unification with their mouth: "et YHVH" - the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as we explained above - and thus he is found to fulfill deed, speech, and thought, which correspond to the three names Y-B-K [Yud-Bet-Kuf], as will be explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:61: And of one who repairs his days with these repairs mentioned, it is said (Psalms 34:13), "who desires life, loves days, to see good" - and the matter may be understood from what they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 224a): that the days which a person repairs are the garment in which his soul is clothed, and through the garment of days he merits to gaze upon and delight in the good hidden away for the righteous - in these words: we have learned, happy are the righteous whose days are meritorious, and remain meritorious for the World to Come; and when they depart, they all join together and become garments of glory to be clothed in, and with that garment they merit to delight in the delight of the World to Come, and with that garment they are destined to be revived and to arise. And all those who have a garment shall arise, this is what is written (Job 38:14), "and they stand up as a garment." Woe to those wicked of the world whose days are deficient through the sins of the ages, and nothing remains of them to be covered with when they depart the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:62: We have learned: all those righteous ones who merited to be clothed in the glory of their days are aroused in that world with the crowns with which the Patriarchs are crowned, from that river which flows and goes forth to the Garden of Eden, this is what is written (Isaiah 58:11), "and the LORD shall guide you continually, and satisfy your soul in drought," and so on; but those wicked of the world who did not merit to be clothed in the garment of their days - of them it is written (Jeremiah 17:6), "and shall be like a tamarisk in the desert, and shall not see when good comes, but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:63: Behold, it says that through the garment of days one delights in the delight of the World to Come, and is crowned from that river which flows and goes forth - and through this the verse "who loves days" may be understood: since the days are the garments in which his soul is clothed, one must love the days, for just as a person loves the garment in which his body is clothed - for without that garment he would be naked - so, insofar as it concerns the repair of his soul, he should love the days, which are the garments in which his soul is clothed - and this is "to see good," for through the garment of days he attains to gaze upon and delight in the good of the World to Come, as explained in the discourse; and the proof is the reality of the perception the righteous will attain of the light hidden away for the righteous, as it is said (Psalms 27:13), "had I not believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living." And he said "to see," for a person sees only through light, and that hidden light is the true sight by which Adam the first man gazed from one end of the world to the other, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 12a), and elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 31b) on the virtues of that light.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:64: And when he contemplates what has been said, he must repair himself through his Torah and his commandments day by day, as the verse says (Deuteronomy 24:15), "on his day you shall give him his wage, and the sun shall not set upon it" - meaning, that he give to the day itself its own wage, namely its repair through Torah and commandments, and "the sun shall not set upon it," for over every single day there is an appointed angel, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, page 92a), concerning the reason one must fast for a bad dream on the very day, even on Shabbat - see there. And concerning this: the day that has passed without repair is gone and lost. And for this reason it is also said (Avot chapter 2), "repent one day before your death," so that all his days be in repentance, as explained in the Gate of Fear. And should one wish to say, "tomorrow I will repair and read" - we have already found the like of this in the Gemara (cf. Eruvin 65b): "day-laborers do not borrow by day and repay by night" - one must not delay payment, but pay his debt at once, for if he delays paying day by day, the debt will grow heavy upon him; and the pious one wrote of this matter in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Reckoning, Reckoning 11). And in the Zohar (Parashat Ki Tetze, page 278a) they explained this verse concerning the prayers that ascend above through Metatron. And happy is one who repairs his days in the manner stated, for he will certainly merit the good hidden away.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:1: Since in the previous chapter we were occupied with the matter of the repairs and adornments of the Shechinah, we saw fit to follow it with this chapter, to explain that all the weighty labors a person is obligated to perform for the repair of the Shechinah must be done with joy, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart," and it says (Psalms 100:2), "serve the LORD with joy" - and they explained in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Vayechi, page 216b), in these words: Rabbi Yosi said, the Shechinah rests only in a whole place, not in a deficient place, nor a flawed place, nor a sad place, but in a place of joyful intent - and therefore, all those years that Joseph was separated from his father and Jacob was sad, the Shechinah did not rest upon him. We have learned, Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Abba: it is written, "serve the LORD with joy, come before Him with singing" - to exclude that there is no service of the Holy One, blessed be He, except from within joy, for Rabbi Elazar said, the Shechinah does not rest from within sadness, as it is written (2 Kings 3:15), "but now bring me a minstrel; and it came to pass, when the minstrel played" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:2: And I heard in the name of our teacher Rabbi Isaac Luria Ashkenazi, peace be upon him, that he explained the verse "because you did not serve," and so on, "from the abundance of all" - meaning, all the more so if you had an abundance of everything. And the intent is, that he should rejoice in the joy of the Holy One, blessed be He, and in His commandments and His Torah, more than in all the wealth of the world - just as it is said of the Torah (Proverbs 3:15), "and all your desires cannot compare to her" - so no joy in the world can compare to the joy of a commandment; and so he explained above, in chapter 2, concerning love. And along these lines I heard in the name of Rabbi Yonah, peace be upon him, on the verse (Proverbs 3:9), "honor the LORD with your wealth" - that he explained it as "more than your wealth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:3: And the ways for a person to acquire joy in his heart: when he considers the goodness of the Creator, blessed be He, toward him, as we have elaborated - whether in the giving of the Torah, and so on - and say in his heart: the Cause of all causes and the Source of all sources, who created and brought into being all existing things for the sake of man, His particular providence is upon me - even though His greatness has no end or limit, He watches over a tiny gnat like me, who am considered as nothing before His greatness, blessed be He, to do good to me with the goods of this world and the goods of the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:4: And this is like the parable of a king who has ministers and dignitaries beyond number, and he saw in his kingdom a certain servant, and called him and said to him: I wish that you serve me and be among the ministers who stand before me, seeing the king's face; and he said to him, if you serve me properly, I will set your rank above the honored ministers who are with me. Is it not fitting for that servant to serve his master's service with joy, and say in his heart: since the king, with his greatness and dominion, lacking nothing, chose me for my own benefit, that I should serve before him, it is fitting that I perform my service before him only with joy and gladness of heart.
